synopsis: Chapter 12 identifies the UK Treasury and Department for Transport as organisations that apply reference-class-based optimism-bias uplifts as documented practice [f9605]. The glossary confirms that the Treasury applies these uplifts to public projects and connects the practice to cost and schedule risk analysis [f16314, f16437]. Separately, the Treasury Five Case Model structures a business case into strategic, economic, commercial, financial and management cases [f16459]. The supplied facts give no uplift percentages or implementation dates, and do not specify how the uplifts fit within the Five Case Model [f9605, f16314, f16437, f16459].

relations.note: Both identify Treasury use of reference-class-based uplifts; the glossary specifies public projects.
The glossary connects the documented optimism-bias practice to cost and schedule risk analysis.
Adds the optimism-bias label and cost-and-schedule risk context to Treasury uplifts.
